k.du.khana1: In the name of Allah (I begin).
k.du.khana2: Thanks to Allah who fed me this and gave it to me, without any power of my own.
k.du.sona: O Allah! With Your name I sleep and I wake up.
k.du.neend: Thanks to Allah who woke us up after sleep, and to Him we will return.
k.du.bath1: In the name of Allah. O Allah! I seek Your protection from dirty and bad things.
k.du.bath2: O Allah! I ask for Your forgiveness.
k.du.nikalna: In the name of Allah, I trust in Allah; all strength comes only from Allah.
k.du.jazak: May Allah reward you with good! (The best way to say thank you)

k.storiesHint: Read or listen to a story, and remember the lesson 🌟
k.quizScore: MashaAllah! {n}/3 right on the first try ⭐
k.noImg: No pictures are made of the Prophets or the Sahaba — only the story and its lesson.
k.alim: Stories and duas are taken from the Quran and authentic hadith — please confirm with a scholar.
k.s.nuh.b: For many years, Prophet Nuh (AS) kindly invited his people to Allah.|Allah told him to build a big ark.|Then lots of rain came, and there was water everywhere.|Everyone who listened to Allah and got into the ark, along with pairs of animals, was kept safe.
k.s.nuh.m: Listening to Allah is always good.
k.s.yunus.t: Prophet Yunus (AS) and the big fish
k.s.yunus.b: Prophet Yunus (AS) fell from a ship into the sea.|A big fish swallowed him.|In the darkness inside the fish, he called to Allah: “La ilaha illa Anta, Subhanaka, inni kuntu minaz-zalimeen.”|Allah heard his dua and brought him out safely.
k.s.yunus.m: Remember Allah when things are hard — He always hears.
k.s.naml.t: Prophet Sulaiman (AS) and the little ant
k.s.naml.b: Prophet Sulaiman (AS) was marching with his army.|A little ant said: “O ants! Go into your homes so you are not crushed!”|Prophet Sulaiman (AS) heard her, smiled, and thanked Allah.|He did not harm the ants at all.
k.s.naml.m: Care for even the smallest creatures, and thank Allah.
k.s.dog.t: The thirsty dog and the water
k.s.dog.b: Our Prophet ﷺ told a story.|A man on a journey became very thirsty; he climbed down into a well and drank water.|When he came out, he saw a dog licking wet mud because it was so thirsty.|He filled his leather sock with water and gave the dog a drink. Allah liked this so much that He forgave the man.
k.s.dog.m: Be kind to animals — Allah loves those who show mercy.
k.s.camel.b: Once our Prophet ﷺ went into a garden.|There was a camel there that began to cry when it saw him.|The Prophet ﷺ gently stroked its head and it became calm.|Then he told the camel's owner: fear Allah about this animal, do not keep it hungry and do not overwork it.
k.s.camel.m: Animals are Allah's creation too — be gentle with them.
k.s.ibrahim.b: The people of Prophet Ibrahim (AS) worshipped idols made of stone.|He kindly explained that idols can neither hear nor help anyone.|One day, when the people went out, he broke the idols and left only the biggest one.|When they asked, he said: “Ask this big one, if they can speak!” They understood the idols could do nothing, but they stayed stubborn.|They threw Prophet Ibrahim (AS) into a fire.|Allah commanded: “O fire! Be cool and safe for Ibrahim.” And he was completely safe.
k.s.ibrahim.m: Worship Allah alone and stand firmly for the truth — Allah protects.
k.s.ibrahim.q2: Which idol did Prophet Ibrahim (AS) leave?
k.s.ibrahim.q3o: It got even hotter|It became cool and safe|Nothing happened
k.s.yusuf.b: Out of jealousy, Prophet Yusuf's (AS) brothers threw him into a well.|A caravan took him to Egypt. He faced many hardships there, even prison, but he stayed patient and truthful.|Allah honoured him and he became the keeper of Egypt's stores.|Years later there was a famine, and the same brothers came to him for grain.|Prophet Yusuf (AS) could have taken revenge, but he said: “No blame on you today. May Allah forgive you.”
k.s.yusuf.m: Forgiving, even when you could take revenge, is a very great good deed.
k.s.yusuf.q1: Where did the brothers throw Prophet Yusuf (AS)?
k.s.yusuf.q1o: Into a well|Into a river|Into a forest
k.s.yusuf.q2: What did he do in hard times?
k.s.yusuf.q3: What did he do when the brothers came?
k.s.musa.b: Pharaoh was a cruel king who treated the Children of Israel unjustly.|By Allah's command, Prophet Musa (AS) left at night with his people.|The sea was in front and Pharaoh's army was behind. The people panicked: “We will be caught!”|Prophet Musa (AS) said with full certainty: “Never! My Lord is with me; He will guide me.”|Allah told him to strike the sea with his staff — the sea split and a dry path appeared in the middle.|Everyone crossed safely.
k.s.musa.m: Even when every way seems closed, trust Allah.
k.s.musa.q2o: We are caught|My Lord is with me|Let's go back
k.s.musa.q3o: It froze into ice|A dry path opened in the middle|Nothing happened
k.s.bilal.b: Bilal (RA) was a slave in Makkah.|When he accepted Islam, his master hurt him badly — he made him lie on hot sand and put a heavy rock on him.|Through all the pain he kept saying: “Ahad, Ahad!” — Allah is One!|Abu Bakr (RA) bought him and set him free.|Later the Prophet ﷺ chose him to call the adhan — the adhan rang out in his strong voice.
k.s.bilal.m: Hold firmly to your faith, even when it is hard.
k.s.bilal.q1: What did Bilal (RA) say when he was hurt?
k.s.bilal.q3: What job did the Prophet ﷺ later choose him for?
k.s.guest.t: The lamp that was put out
k.s.guest.b: Once a hungry guest came to the Prophet ﷺ.|One of the Ansar Sahaba took him home, but there was only enough food for the children.|They lovingly put the children to sleep and put out the lamp at mealtime, so the guest would think they were eating too.|The guest ate until he was full, and the family slept hungry.|In the morning the Prophet ﷺ said that Allah was very pleased with what they did, and a verse of the Quran came down: “They prefer others over themselves, even when they are in need.”
k.s.guest.m: Putting others before yourself is very beloved to Allah.
k.s.guest.q1: How much food was in the house?
k.s.guest.q1o: Lots|Only enough for the children|None at all
k.s.guest.q2: Why did they put out the lamp?
k.s.guest.q2o: To go to sleep|So the guest could eat his fill comfortably|To save oil
k.s.guest.q3o: Nothing|He was pleased and sent down a verse|He sent another guest
k.s.kab.b: Ka'b ibn Malik (RA) stayed behind from a journey (the expedition of Tabuk) without any excuse.|When the Prophet ﷺ returned, some people made up false excuses.|Ka'b (RA) thought: I will not lie. He honestly said that he had no excuse.|For a while things were very hard for him, but he kept patiently repenting.|Then Allah announced in the Quran that his repentance was accepted. He said: “Allah saved me because of the truth.”
k.s.kab.m: Tell the truth, even when it feels hard — truth leads to success.
k.s.kab.q1o: Made a false excuse|Honestly told the truth|Hid away
k.s.kab.q2: What did he do in the hard time?
k.s.kab.q2o: Was patient and repented|Got angry|Left the city
k.s.kab.q3o: Allah accepted his repentance|Nothing happened|Everyone forgot
